title: Western Carriers (India) Ltd - 544258 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Western Carriers is a rail-based logistics operator, not a cables maker, so subsector is a poor fit; Q4 EXIM containers fell 3.2% YoY and 11% QoQ, EBITDA margin slipped to 5%, and management gave no numbers but promised sequential improvement.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

financial_highlights.change: +4% QoQ from INR478 crore in Q3
down from INR27 crore in Q3
down from INR10.8 crore in Q3; margin 1.7% vs 2.3%

financial_highlights.value: over INR70 crore (management cited INR74 crore in Q&A)

segments.name: EXIM
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 34,404 containers, down 10.96% QoQ and 3.17% YoY; FY26 volume 1,40,225, up about 5% YoY. Management says the company held up better than the industry, which saw about a 40% fall in March. Growth is shifting to East Coast ports.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 23,350 containers, up 17.79% YoY and down less than 1% QoQ, helped by pivots to chemicals, FMCG, aggregates and salt. FY26 volume 86,353, up 8.16% YoY.

segments.name: Devaliya MMCT (Morbi)
segments.commentary: 32-acre multimodal terminal now fully operational. Tiles throughput fell sharply in March due to propane and natural gas shortages affecting about 700 units; volumes are rising month-on-month in industrial chemicals.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal numerical guidance. It expects EBITDA margin to recover from about 4.6-4.7% toward roughly 7%, which it says was the FY25 level.
Management expects sequential improvement in both top line and bottom line from Q1 FY27, and says it is comfortable with the trend in May.
Management targets debtor days below 120 in FY27.
FY27 capex planned at INR100 crore, of which INR92 crore is said to be funded from remaining IPO proceeds; spend is tied to customer orders and will be calibrated to EXIM normalisation.
Management expects operating cash flow to improve as realisations and EXIM volumes recover.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was over INR70 crore (about INR74 crore per Q&A), spent on specialised containers, reach stackers, commercial vehicles and handling equipment.
The company procured 161 specialised containers in FY26; a further order of similar size is under production and is expected to enter operations from the end of May 2026 over the next 1-1.5 quarters.
Own specialised container fleet is over 1,000 units.
Devaliya MMCT (32 acres, Morbi) is fully operational; fixed rail services run from Devaliya to CMLK, Bangalore, Chennai, Calcutta and Guwahati at lower frequency.
FY27 capex of INR100 crore covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles, reach stackers, forklifts and large cranes.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is strong, with pedigreed customers for the rest of the year, and that the East Coast EXIM pipeline is robust.
Domestic demand for specialised containers is strong, with similar orders in the pipeline for FY27.

Industry-wide, about 40-45k Indian containers were stranded at March end; freight rates, war-risk surcharges and insurance costs rose sharply, with war-risk surcharges nearly doubling ocean freight in some cases.
Capacity on US and Europe routes is about 30-35% of normal; Cape of Good Hope diversions add about 3,500 nautical miles and 10-15 days.
Realisations were hit by geopolitical factors and are expected to improve as EXIM volumes recover.

Receivables have risen, with the company citing growth in retail MMCT customers (up 25-30% YoY) who pay only when the next consignment ships. Management said the company had INR600+ crore in receivables, a figure raised by an analyst and not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from INR172 crore to INR217 crore despite IPO net proceeds of about INR363 crore, of which about INR163 crore went to debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects working capital needs as the new Devaliya MMCT became operational.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a revenue split between rail, road and water?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue, saying it operates as a consolidated multimodal logistics provider and that splitting would distort the picture.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and when will cash flow turn positive, given negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26 and a planned INR100 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets debtor days below 120 this year, says INR100 crore of IPO funds is still unspent, and expects realisations and cash flow to improve as EXIM recovers. It said the EXIM trade should improve within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What further margin pressure is coming from April pricing, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numerical guidance, but said margins should improve sequentially, with EBITDA margin targeted back toward 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the INR100 crore capex go and what are the domestic growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles and heavy equipment. Domestic growth is expected to come from the Morbi MMLP, tiles volumes once propane supply returns, and Western seaboard clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers of the ROE/ROCE decline and the outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ROE and ROCE to return to strong double-digit levels as margins recover from 4.6-4.7%, citing a debt position it considers under control.

risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed (traffic about 5% of pre-war levels); the timing of EXIM normalisation is uncertain.
Tiles and steel demand in Morbi depends on propane and gas supply; about 700 units are affected.
Rising receivables and negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26, with debt up to INR217 crore.
Container detention, demurrage and empty-wagon running (15-20% vs a 5% norm) could keep costs high.
Watch whether debtor days fall below 120 and whether the Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improves from 5.0%.
Watch the pace of FY27 capex against the INR100 crore plan and its funding.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident about recovery and long-term prospects but gave no numerical guidance. It was cautious about near-term EXIM and margins, and avoided segment margin and revenue-split questions.
key_quotes: Our numbers are 57,754 containers compared to 55,356 containers in Q4 of last year, which is an absolute increase of 2,398 containers and 4.3% increase.
We are targeting to bring our debtor days to below 120 in this current financial year.
I feel that from here our EBITDA margins should sequentially keep improving because we've seen three wars back-to-back in the last year and a half.
